blocks.text: Recall that X_i and Y_j have size at most d' coloneqq max d_A, d_B. Run on them for some parameter p ge 1 to be determined later. Let m=O(p^2) denote the number of parts in each returned partition. We call a Delta -approximate exact triangle (i, k, j) A -exceptional if A[i,k] is covered by some x in X_i^*, and B -exceptional if B[k,j] is covered by some y in Y_j^*, and ordinary otherwise. The running time of this setup is bounded by the running time of, that is, tilde O(n^2d'p^3) = tilde O(n^2dtp^3)

blocks.heading: Uniformization.
blocks.text: start-of-enumerate:. (Exceptional Triangles) We will explicitly enumerate all exceptional Delta -approximate exact triangles. We describe how to enumerate all A -exceptional Delta -approximate exact triangles and omit the analogous proof for B -exceptional triangles (including exchanging the roles of d_A and d_B ). First, apply for all (i, j) in [n]^2 to obtain a set P_(i, j) that is a 3Delta -cover for P_(24d'/p)^(pm 3Delta)(X_i^*, Y_j) where each element in P_(i, j) covers sums from at least 12d'/p pairs in X_i^*times Y_j up to pm 3Delta and each element is covered by at most 2 numbers in P_(i, j). We then call such a triangle (i, k, j) popular if -C[i,j] = z pm 6Delta for some z in P_(i, j) and unpopular otherwise. We solve both cases separately. start-of-enumerate:. (Popular Triangles) In this case, we simply use that the number of pairs (i, j) supporting popular exceptional triangles is bounded. If P_(i, j)neemptyset, any one of its centers covers sums from at least 12d'/p pairs in an interval of width 6Delta. Partition this interval into six intervals of width Delta; one contains sums from at least 2d'/p pairs. Any sum in this subinterval belongs to P_(2d'/p)^(pmDelta)(X_i^*, Y_j). Therefore, we know by definition of X^*_i (property (ii) of ) that the number of nonempty P_(i, j) is at most n^2/p. For each such pair, we enumerate all possible k in [n] and store the triangle (i, k, j) in T. The running time of this step is clearly bounded by O(n^3/p).. (Unpopular Triangles) We enumerate all pairs (i, j) in [n]^2 where -C[i,j] is not covered by P_(i, j) up to pm 6 Delta. We enumerate all x in X_i^* and test if a suitable y exists that satisfies x + y = -C[i,j] pm 3Delta. If it does, we list all k with A[i,k] = x pm Delta and insert (i, k, j) into T. For the running time, suppose that A[i,k] + B[k,j] + C[i,j] = 0 pm Delta where A[i,k] = x pm Delta, B[k,j] = y pm Delta for some x in X_i^* and y in Y_j, and no z in P_(i, j) satisfies -C[i,j] = z pm 6Delta. This implies that x + y = - C[i,j] pm 3Delta. On the other hand, since -C[i,j] is not covered by P_(i, j) up to pm 6Delta, fewer than 48d'/p pairs (x, y)in X_i^*times Y_j satisfy x+y=-C[i,j]pm3Delta. Otherwise, one half of this width- 6Delta interval would contain sums from at least 24d'/p pairs; any one of those sums would belong to P_(24d'/p)^(pm3Delta)(X_i^*, Y_j) and hence have a cover center in P_(i, j) within 6Delta of -C[i,j]. Notice that for each pair (i, j) we list d_A le d values x and in total at most O(d'/p) many pairs (x, y). For each such pair (x, y) we enumerate at most O(n/d_A) values of k. The time for this step is hence bounded by O ens*( n^2 ens*( d + frac(d')(p)cdot frac(n)(d_A) ) ) = O ens*( n^2 ens*( d + frac(nt)(p) ) ) = O ens*( n^2d + frac(n^3t)(p) ). end-of-enumerate. (Ordinary Triangles) Enumerate all pairs g, h in [m]. Define matrices A_g, B_h, and C_(g, h) as A_g[i,k] &coloneqq mathmakebox[2.8cm][l](A[i,k] - s_(i, g)) &text(if A[i,k] = x pm Delta for some x in X_(i, g), ) &text(otherwise; ) B_h[k,j] &coloneqq mathmakebox[2.8cm][l](B[k,j] - t_(j, h)) &text(if B[k,j] = y pm Delta for some y in Y_(j, h), ) &text(otherwise; ) C_(g, h)[i,j] &coloneqq mathmakebox[2.8cm][l](C[i,j] + s_(i, g) + t_(j, h)) &text(if C[i,j] ne bot, ) &text(otherwise. ) We can assume that each triangle appears in only one instance since each number is only covered by one element of a Delta -cover ( ). Moreover, the value of the triangle is unchanged since all s_(i, g) and t_(j, h) cancel: A_g[i,k] + B_h[k,j] + C_(g, h)[i,j] = A[i,k] + B[k,j] + C[i,j]. Now, we can verify that A_g and B_h are (d', 2Delta) -uniform: The set X_(A_g) of all non- bot entries in A_g is covered by the 2Delta -cover S_g, by, property (i). Similarly, all non- bot entries in B_h are covered by the 2Delta -cover T_h. Since |S_g|, |T_h| le d', each matrix has a 2Delta -cover of size at most d' and hence a Delta -cover of size at most 2d', by splitting each covering interval into two. Let qge1 be another parameter to be determined later. In the following, we modify C_(g, h) to also become (O(d'q), Delta) -uniform to make the whole instance (A_g, B_h, C_(g, h)) uniform. Define the set P coloneqq set(z in Real: abs(set((x, y) in S_g times T_h: x + y + z = 0 pm 5Delta)) ge d'/q). We can compute P in time tilde O(|S_g| |T_h|) = tilde O(d'^2), represented as a union of intervals. Each membership query in P can then be answered in time O(log n). We call a pair (i, j) popular if C_(g, h)[i,j] in P and unpopular otherwise. We solve both cases separately. start-of-enumerate:. (Popular Entries) Let C_(g, h)^( pop ) be the restriction of C_(g, h) to the popular entries with all unpopular entries replaced by bot. To bound its cover size, take a maximal subset Qsubseteq P whose points are more than 10Delta apart. The intervals of width 10Delta around points of Q are disjoint, and each contains negated sums from at least d'/q pairs, so |Q|le |S_g||T_h|/(d'/q). By maximality, Q is a 10Delta -cover of P; splitting each interval into two gives a 5Delta -cover. Observe that |P|_(pm 5Delta) le O(|S_g||T_h|/(d'/q)) = O(d'q) and therefore P also has a Delta -cover of size O(d'q). Hence, the instance (A_g, B_h, C_(g, h)^( pop )) is (O(d'q), Delta) -uniform. We can trivially reduce this further to O((d'q/d)^3)=O((tq)^3) instances that are (d, Delta) -uniform, which we store in I. There are m^2=O(p^4) possible choices for (g, h), so the total running time of this step is tilde O(p^4t^3q^3n^2).. (Unpopular Entries) In this case, we enumerate all unpopular pairs (i, j). By the definition of P, fewer than d'/q pairs (x, y) in S_g times T_h satisfy x + y + C_(g, h)[i,j] = 0 pm 5Delta. We enumerate all x in S_g and test whether there is y in T_h satisfying this condition. If there is, we list all k with A_g[i, k] = x pm 2Delta and insert (i, k, j) into T. For correctness, every Delta -approximate exact triangle (i, k, j) in this instance has representatives x in S_g and y in T_h with A_g[i, k] = x pm 2Delta and B_h[k, j] = y pm 2Delta. Together with A_g[i, k] + B_h[k, j] + C_(g, h)[i, j] = 0 pmDelta, this gives x + y + C_(g, h)[i, j] = 0 pm 5Delta, so we certainly list k and thus include (i, k, j) into T. For the running time, notice that for each pair (i, j), we list d' values of x and in total at most O(d'/q) pairs (x, y). For each such pair, we enumerate at most O(n/d_A) values of k. The total time of this step is hence bounded by tilde O ens*(p^4n^2 ens*(d' + frac(d')(q)cdot frac(n)(d_A))) = tilde O ens*(p^4n^2 ens*(dt + frac(d_At)(q)cdot frac(n)(d_A))) = tilde O ens*(n^2dtp^4 + frac(n^3tp^4)(q) ). end-of-enumerate end-of-enumerate

blocks.heading: Uniform to Uniform Regular
blocks.text: start-of-lemma: [Reduction from Approximately Low-Rank to Approximately Uniform and Regular Instances] For any t ge 1, Delta ge 0, there is a potential-adjusting reduction from a Real Exact Triangle instance (A, B, C) where one matrix has Delta -approximate rank- r to t^(875)n^(o(1)) instances that are (r, Delta) -uniform and (1/r, Delta) -regular. The reduction runs in time ens*(rt^(875)n^2 + n^3 (t))^(1+o(1)). end-of-lemma start-of-proof: We use the exact same proof as in [Fischer26] modulo the approximate versions of rank, slice-uniform, uniform, and regular. start-of-enumerate:. (Low-Rank to Slice-Uniform) Run the potential-adjusting reduction from with some parameter t_ sl to transform the low-rank instance into (r, Delta) -slice-uniform instances. Denote the output by ( I_ sl, T_ sl ). This step runs in time tilde O(n^3/t_ sl + n^2rt_ sl ^2).. (Slice-Uniform to Uniform) We further reduce each of the obtained instances (A', B', C') in I_ sl into (r, Delta) -uniform instances ( I', T') by running with some parameter t_ unif. Let I_ unif be the union of all I' and T_ unif the union of all T'. This reduction is still potential-adjusting and runs in time tilde O( I_ sl cdot (n^3/t_ unif + n^2rt_ unif ^(41))).. (Uniform to Uniform Regular) We reduce the instances in I_ unif further to regular instances I_ reg. Set initially I_ reg gets emptyset. In this reduction step we will miss some Delta -approximate exact triangles, but we ensure that each such triangle is present in one of the instances (A_ sm, B, C), (A, B_ sm, C), or (A, B, C_ sm ) that we will construct. We will guarantee that these remaining instances have low approximate rank, so we will maintain low- Delta -approximate-rank decompositions of A_ sm, B_ sm, and C_ sm. Initially, we set every entry of these matrices equal to bot and start with a trivial Delta -approximate rank-0 decomposition. Enumerate the instances (A', B', C') in I_ unif. Since they are obtained from potential-adjusting reductions, we also know potential adjustments u and v such that A'[i,k] = A[i,k] + u[i] + v[k] quad text(or) quad A'[i,k] = bot for all entries. Let q be a parameter determined later. Let X_i be the greedy minimum Delta -cover of the entries of the i -th row of A', with |X_i|le r, and let Y_k be the corresponding cover for the k -th column. In each cover the centers are more than 2Delta apart, so every non- bot entry belongs to a unique cover interval, which we call its bucket. We call an entry A'[i,k] row-heavy if the element x in X_i with x = A'[i,k] pm Delta covers more than a q/r fraction of the entries of the i -th row, that is, k': A'[i,k'] = x pmDelta > nq/r. Similarly, we call an entry column-heavy if its center yin Y_k satisfies i': A'[i', k] = y pmDelta > nq/r. Otherwise, we call A'[i,k] light. Let A' = A'_text(row) sqcup A'_text(col) sqcup A'_text(light) denote the partition of the entries of A' into row-heavy, column-heavy, and light entries. Entries that are both row-heavy and column-heavy are assigned arbitrarily to either part. Do the same for B' and C'. We proceed in two substeps. start-of-enumerate:. (Light Entries) Each row or column bucket contains at most nq/r light entries. An interval of width 2Delta intersects at most two consecutive cover intervals, since their centers are more than 2Delta apart. In each row, split the light entries of every bucket into O(q) groups of size at most n/(2r). Do the same independently for columns, and partition A'_ light according to the pairs of groups. This gives O(q^2) matrices that are (1/r, Delta) -regular. Hence, we can transform the subinstance (A'_ light, B'_ light, C'_ light ) into O(q^6) instances that are (r, Delta) -uniform and (1/r, Delta) -regular in a potential-adjusting way. We insert all of these instances into I_ reg. This step clearly runs in time tilde O( I_ unif cdot q^6n^2).. (Heavy Entries) Focus on the row-heavy entries of A' for now. For each such entry A'[i,k], we will update A_ sm gets A[i,k] and now also update its rank decomposition. Let X_i^( heavy ) subseteq X_i consist of the centers whose buckets contain more than nq/r entries of the i -th row of A'. Since these buckets are disjoint, |X_i^( heavy )|le r/q. This set Delta -covers the i -th row of A'_ row. Therefore, we can trivially compute a Delta -approximate rank- (r/q) decomposition (U', V', S') of A'_ row. We adjust this decomposition by U[i,ell] &coloneqq U'[i,ell] - u[i], V[ell,k] &coloneqq V'[ell,k] - v[k], which leads to a Delta -approximate rank decomposition (U, V, S = S') of the same rank of the restriction of A to the row-heavy entries of A'. Indeed, for each row-heavy entry (i, k), we have A[i,k] &= A'[i,k] - u[i] - v[k] &= U'[i, S'[i,k]] + V'[S'[i,k], k] - u[i] - v[k] pmDelta &= U[i, S[i,k]] + V[S[i,k], k] pmDelta. We perform the same update-procedure for the column-heavy entries to update A_ sm. We do the same symmetrically for B_ sm and C_ sm. This step runs in time tilde O( I_ unif cdot n^2). end-of-enumerate. (Recursion) Finally, we recurse on the three instances (A_ sm, B, C), (A, B_ sm, C), and (A, B, C_ sm ), which is possible since we have maintained approximate rank decompositions of the three matrices A_ sm, B_ sm, and C_ sm. Denote the recursive outputs by ( I_A, T_A), ( I_B, T_B), and ( I_C, T_C). We return ( I, T) coloneqq ( I_A cup I_B cup I_C cup I_ reg, T_A cup T_B cup T_C cup T_ sl cup T_ unif ). end-of-enumerate This completes the algorithm description. Each step runs in the same time bound as the corresponding step in [Lemma 4.10, Fischer26]. Therefore, the recursion analysis as well as the rank of subinstances is identical to [Fischer26]. The same is true for the choice of parameters t_ sl, t_ unif, q. Thus, we omit further details here. end-of-proof

blocks.heading: Uniform Regular to Uniform Small-Doubling
blocks.text: In this section, we will need some more lemmas corresponding to statements from additive combinatorics but for Delta -approximate reals. Therefore, let us introduce some notation and preliminary statements first to transfer the exact statements easily to the approximate setting. When Delta in Realnneg is clear from context, define for any set Asubseteq Real the set round A coloneqq Delta cdot lfloor a / Delta rfloor: a in A, that is, the set of numbers in A rounded down to an integer multiple of Delta. (For Delta = 0, define round A coloneqq A. )

blocks.heading: Uniform Regular to Uniform Small-Doubling
blocks.text: start-of-lemma: Let Delta in Realnneg and A subseteq Real. Then, we have cabs(A) le abs(round A) le 3cabs(A). end-of-lemma start-of-proof: Notice that any pair of numbers x, y in Real that are rounded to the same number Delta cdot lfloor x/Deltarfloor = Delta cdot lfloor y/Deltarfloor satisfy x = y pm Delta. Thus, the rounded values themselves form a Delta -cover of A. On the other hand, for any x', y' in Real satisfying x' = y' pm Delta the rounded numbers lfloor x'/Deltarfloor and lfloor y'/Deltarfloor differ by at most 1. Consequently, each interval in a Delta -cover of A contains points from at most three rounding bins. This shows for any set A subseteq Real that cabs(A) le abs(round A) le 3cabs(A). qedhere end-of-proof

blocks.heading: Uniform Regular to Uniform Small-Doubling
blocks.text: start-of-lemma: Let Delta in Realnneg and A, B subseteq Real. Then, we have abs(round A + round B) le 4abs(round(A+B)) quad text(and) quad abs(round(A+B)) le 4abs(round A + round B). end-of-lemma start-of-proof: Let a in A and b in B. Simple calculations yield floor(frac(a)(Delta)) + floor(frac(b)(Delta)) le frac(a)(Delta) + frac(b)(Delta) = frac(a+b)(Delta) le floor(frac(a+b)(Delta)) + 1 and floor(frac(a + b)(Delta)) le frac(a + b)(Delta) = frac(a)(Delta) + frac(b)(Delta) le floor(frac(a)(Delta)) + floor(frac(b)(Delta)) + 2. This shows that the number in round A + round B corresponds to at most 4 numbers in A+ B and vice versa. Hence, we get abs(round A + round B) le 4abs(round(A+B)) quad text(and) quad abs(round(A+B)) le 4abs(round A + round B). qedhere end-of-proof

blocks.text: start-of-lemma: [Reduction from Approx. Uniform Regular to Approx. Uniform Low-Doubling Instances] Let Delta in Realnneg and K ge 1. There is a potential-adjusting reduction from a Real Exact Triangle Instance (A, B, C) that is (D, Delta) -uniform and (1/D, Delta) -regular to O(K^(1/56)) instances that are (D, Delta) -uniform and (K, Delta) -doubling. It runs in time tilde O ens*(n^2K^(1/56) + n^3 (K^(1/56))). end-of-lemma start-of-proof: Denote by X the greedy minimum Delta -cover of the set of entries of the instance; its centers are more than 2Delta apart. By uniformity, we know that X le D. We apply BSG Covering ( ) with input sets X, X, -X, tolerance 4Delta, size parameter |X|, and some parameter L to be determined later. This results in sets X_1, ldots, X_L, Y_1, ldots, Y_L and R. Since each interval of width 8Delta is covered by four intervals of width 2Delta, the returned sets satisfy |X_ell+Y_ell|_(pmDelta)le4|X_ell+Y_ell|_(pm4Delta)le O(L^5D) and |R|le O(D^2/L). For each Delta -approximate exact triangle with representatives x, y, zin X, we have x+y=-zpm4Delta. Therefore, its representative pair (x, y) is either in the structured part (if (x, y) in X_ell times Y_ell for some ell ) or in the remainder if (x, y) in R. We deal with both types of triangles separately. start-of-enumerate:. (Remainder) We explicitly list all Delta -approximate exact triangles in the remainder. Enumerate all pairs (x, y) in R and enumerate all k in [n]. Then, enumerate all i in [n] with A[i,k] = x pm Delta and all j in [n] with B[k,j] = y pm Delta. We store all triangles enumerated this way in T. Clearly, we enumerate all triangles in the remainder. For the running time, recall that the instance is (1/D, Delta) -regular, hence for a fixed k and x, there are at most n/D valid choices of i, and similarly for y and j. Therefore, the running time is bounded by tilde O ens*(abs(R)cdot n cdot frac(n)(D)cdot frac(n)(D)) = tilde O ens*(frac(n^3)(L)).. (Structured Part) Enumerate all ell in [L]. First discard from X_ell every center whose interval of width 2Delta contains no entry of A, and do the same for Y_ell and B. We compute the set X_ell + Y_ell by brute-force and construct the matrices A_ell[i,k] &coloneqq mathmakebox[1cm](A[i,k]) &text(if A[i,k] = x pm Delta for some x in X_ell, ) &text(otherwise; ) B_ell[k,j] &coloneqq mathmakebox[1cm](B[k,j]) &text(if B[k,j] = y pm Delta for some y in Y_ell, ) &text(otherwise; ) C_ell[i,j] &coloneqq mathmakebox[1cm](C[i,j]) &text(if C[i,j] = -z pm 3Delta for some z in X_ell + Y_ell, ) &text(otherwise. ) This way, each Delta -approximate exact triangle in the structured part appears in some instance (A_ell, B_ell, C_ell). We further distinguish two cases. start-of-enumerate:. (Sparse Case: X_ell le D/L^2 or Y_ell le D/L^2 ) In this case, one of the matrices A_ell or B_ell is sparse. Suppose X_ell le D/L^2. Then, all entries in A_ell are covered by a Delta -cover of size at most D/L^2 and each element in the cover covers at most a 1/D -fraction of the entries, by regularity. Hence, A_ell can contain at most n^2/L^2 non- bot entries. We can therefore solve the instance (A_ell, B_ell, C_ell) by brute-force and place all triangles in T in time O(n^3/L) across all iterations.. (Dense Case: X_ell > D/L^2 and Y_ell > D/L^2 ) Let W_ell be the set of weights in (A_ell, B_ell, C_ell) and let H_ellcoloneqq X_ellcup Y_ell. The set Z_ell coloneqq ens*( H_ell cup (-(X_ell+Y_ell)) ) + -3Delta, -2Delta, ldots, 3Delta is a Delta -cover of W_ell. Moreover, every center in H_ell is within Delta of a weight in W_ell, by the removal of unused centers. Expanding each interval in a minimum Delta -cover of W_ell to width 4Delta therefore covers H_ell. Each expanded interval contains at most two centers, since these are more than 2Delta apart. Thus H_ell =|H_ell|le2 W_ell. We will bound Z_ell+Z_ell relative to H_ell. First, note that we can bound the approximate doubling of X_ell using Ruzsa's triangle inequality for approximate reals ( ) by cabs(X_ell + X_ell) le 576cdot frac(cabs(X_ell + Y_ell)cabs(X_ell + Y_ell))(cabs(Y_ell)) le O ens*(frac(L^(10)D^2)(D/L^2)) = O(L^(12)D) le O(L^(14))cabs(X_ell). Symmetrically, Y_ell+Y_ell le O(L^(12)D). Since H_ell+H_ell=(X_ell+X_ell)cup(X_ell+Y_ell)cup(Y_ell+Y_ell), it follows that H_ell+H_ell le O(L^(12)D)le O(L^(14)) H_ell. Let Q_ellcoloneqq H_ell. By, we have |Q_ell+Q_ell|le O(L^(14))|Q_ell|. The Plunnecke Ruzsa inequality gives |aQ_ell-bQ_ell|le O(L^(14(a+b)))|Q_ell|, where a, b are nonnegative integers and aQ_ell denotes the a -fold sumset. Every element of Z_ell+Z_ell lies within O(Delta) of an element of (Q_ell+Q_ell)cup(Q_ell-2Q_ell)cup(-4Q_ell), as each term from H_ell contributes less than Delta of rounding error. Consequently, Z_ell+Z_ell le O(L^(56))|Q_ell|le O(L^(56)) H_ell. Since Z_ell Delta -covers W_ell, we obtain cabs(W_ell+W_ell)le3cabs(Z_ell+Z_ell)le O(L^(56))cabs(W_ell). We pick L = Theta(K^(1/56)) such that W_ell has approximate doubling at most K. Therefore, the whole instance (A_ell, B_ell, C_ell) is (K, Delta) -doubling and (D, Delta) -uniform, as desired, and we place it in I. The arguments in this step are just existential, so the total running time across all iterations is bounded by O(n^2L). end-of-enumerate end-of-enumerate This completes the description of the reduction, which is clearly potential-adjusting with I le O(K^(1/56)). For the running time, the initial BSG Covering takes time O(D^2) le O(n^2). The remaining steps are analyzed before. In total, the running time is bounded by tilde O ens*(n^2L + frac(n^3)(L)) = tilde O ens*(n^2K^(1/56) + frac(n^3)(K^(1/56))). qedhere end-of-proof

Given a bipartite graph G subseteq X times Y, with |G| ge alpha n^2, there exist X' subseteq X and Y' subseteq Y such that start-of-enumerate: [label=( )]. for every x' in X', y' in Y', there are Omega(alpha^5n^2) length-3 paths from x' to y', and. |G cap (X' times Y')| ge Omega(alpha|X'|n) ge Omega(alpha^2n^2). end-of-enumerate The sets can be computed in randomized time tilde O((1/alpha)^5|X'| + (1/alpha)n + (1/alpha)^6). end-of-lemma

blocks.text: start-of-lemma: [Single-Set BSG for Approximate Reals] Let Delta in Realnneg and let X, Y subseteq R be Omega(Delta) -spaced sets of size n each. Let G subseteq X times Y be of size G ge alpha n^2 and suppose that x + y: (x, y) in G le n. Then, there are X' subseteq X and Y' subseteq Y such that start-of-enumerate: [label=( )]. X' + Y' le O((1/alpha)^5 n) and. G cap (X' times Y') ge Omega(alpha^2n^2). end-of-enumerate end-of-lemma start-of-proof: Fix a constant c_0ge1 such that X and Y are Delta/c_0 -spaced. Consider the bipartite graph with X and Y as its two sides and edges given by G. Let X' and Y' be the sets given by the graph lemma ( ). We claim that these sets satisfy both claimed properties. Property (ii) immediately follows from, property (ii), so we focus on proving the first property. Let S be a Delta -cover of the set x + y: (x, y) in G of size n. Let T be the greedy minimum Delta -cover of X' + Y', whose centers are more than 2Delta apart. We analyze the following algorithm to bound the size of T: By property (i) of, the innermost step is executed at least Omega(|T| cdot alpha^5|X||Y|) times. Since (x', y), (x, y), and (x, y') are all edges in G and by the definition of S, at least one triple is marked in each iteration. Next, we argue that each element in S^3 is marked O(c_0^2)=O(1) times, bounding the number of total marks by O(|S|^3). This then immediately implies |T| le O ens*( c_0^2|S|^3 (alpha^5 |X||Y|)) = O ens*( n (alpha^5)), and since T is a Delta -cover of X' + Y', we have X' + Y' le O((1/alpha)^5n), property (i). To prove the claim, consider (a, b, c) in S^3 that is marked by some path of length 3 via x', y, x, y'. By adding the conditions on a and c and subtracting the condition on b, we get a - b + c = x' + y' pm 3Delta, and a-b+c = t pm 4Delta. Hence, there can be at most O(1) choices for t in T leading to (a, b, c) being marked. Each choice of t in turn uniquely determines (x', y') in X' times Y'. Furthermore, we know that x = c - y' pm 2Delta and y = a - x' pm 2Delta. The Delta/c_0 spacing gives O(c_0) options each for x and y for a fixed choice of (x', y'). Thus (a, b, c) can be marked at most O(c_0^2)=O(1) times. end-of-proof
